# Plan and Implement

## Change Summary

Updated `CalibrationRun::finish()` so scenario status and `artifact_path` now reflect underlying `HarnessRun` failures in addition to checkpoint classifications, while preserving artifact capture for marginal-only runs. Added a regression test proving a calibration run that fails through shared-harness assertions outside `check_envelope()` now returns a failed `ScenarioRow` with the expected artifact path.

## Steps

1. [Completed] Inspected `CalibrationRun::finish()` and the shared harness failure APIs to confirm how scenario status and artifact paths could diverge from real harness failures.
2. [Completed] Patched `crates/tank_harness/src/calibration.rs` so marginal scenarios still archive artifacts, but any `HarnessRun::finish()` failure now escalates the scenario row to `fail` and exposes the deterministic artifact path.
3. [Completed] Added regression coverage in `crates/tank_harness/tests/calibration_report.rs` for a shared-harness assertion outside checkpoint envelopes, then formatted and reran the targeted calibration-report tests.

## Validation Evidence

- `cargo fmt --all` passed.
- `git diff --check -- crates/tank_harness/src/calibration.rs crates/tank_harness/tests/calibration_report.rs` passed with no whitespace issues.
- `cargo test -p tank_harness --test calibration_report` passed with `8 passed; 0 failed`, including `test_finish_propagates_shared_harness_failures`.

## Outstanding Risks

- I only reran the targeted calibration-report test file for this amendment; the broader workspace test matrix was not rerun in this stage.
- Shared-harness failures are still surfaced only at the scenario level in `ScenarioRow`; checkpoint rows remain unchanged because the current report schema has no dedicated field for non-checkpoint assertion details.
